'''Piramal Finance Limited''' (PFL) is an Indian [[Non-bank financial institution|non-banking financial company]] (NBFC) headquartered in [[Mumbai]], India. Following a corporate restructuring in September 2025, it serves as the consolidated financial services entity of the [[Piramal Group]]. The company was originally incorporated in 1984 as Dewan Housing Finance Corporation (DHFL).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sage Journals: Discover world-class research |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/action/cookieAbsent |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Sage Journals |language=en |doi=10.1177/0972820121998824}}</ref> In 2021, DHFL was acquired by Piramal Capital & Housing Finance for ₹34,250 crore following insolvency proceedings under the [[Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016|Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code]].

In April 2025, the company transitioned from a Housing Finance Company (HFC) designation to an Investment and Credit Company (NBFC-ICC) classification by the [[Reserve Bank of India]] (RBI).<ref>{{cite news |title=Piramal Capital gets RBI nod to operate as NBFC-ICC - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/stocks/piramal-capital-rbi-nod-to-operate-nbfc-icc-to-exit-housing-finance-business-19585590.htm |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=CNBCTV18 |date=7 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref> This shift was followed by an "upper-layer" regulatory classification. In September 2025, the company executed a reverse merger with its parent entity, Piramal Enterprises Limited (PEL), to consolidate the group's financial services business into a single public listed entity. Piramal Finance's credit operations are organized into retail housing, MSME lending, and a "Wholesale 2.0" portfolio that includes real estate and corporate mid-market loans.

== History ==
=== Background and DHFL period (1984–2018) ===
The company was incorporated in 1984 as Dewan Housing Finance Corporation (DHFL).<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=DHFL: Building on current enthusiasm around affordable housing |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/super-50-companies-2017/dhfl-building-on-current-enthusiasm-around-affordable-housing/47659/1 |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=www.forbesindia.com |language=en}}</ref> It expanded through several acquisitions, including the 2010 purchase of [[Deutsche Postbank]]'s Indian home finance unit for ₹1,079 crore and the acquisition of a majority stake in DHFL Pramerica Life Insurance in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dewan Housing Finance Ltd |url=https://www.hdfcsec.com/hsl.research.pdf/DHFC.pdf |website=HDFC Securities}}</ref>

=== Governance failure and insolvency (2019–2021) ===
Between 2019 and 2021, the company underwent a restructuring following allegations of financial impropriety and regulatory intervention.<ref name=":0" /> In January 2019, investigative reports alleged the siphoning of approximately ₹31,000 crore through shell companies, a claim denied by the company's management.<ref name="web.archive.org">{{cite web |title=:: Cobrapost :: |url=https://cobrapost.com/blog/press-realise-dhfl-l/1374 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190129141356/https://cobrapost.com/blog/press-realise-dhfl-l/1374 |archive-date=29 January 2019 |access-date=15 January 2022 |website=cobrapost.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pandey |first=Devesh K. |date=2022-06-22 |title=CBI books DHFL and its promoters for alleged ₹34,615-crore bank fraud |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/cbi-books-dhfl-and-its-promoters-for-alleged-34615-crore-bank-fraud/article65553239.ece |access-date=2026-05-14 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> Despite initial credit rating stability, DHFL defaulted on debt repayments in June 2019, leading to a loss in market valuation.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=30 January 2019 |title=News portal alleges Rs 31,000 crore fraud by home finance company DHFL - Times of India ► |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/news-portal-alleges-rs-31000-crore-fraud-by-home-finance-company-dhfl/articleshow/67748033.cms |access-date=2019-02-05 |website=The Times of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-30 |title=Closely guarded mechanism “Bandra Book” used to divert Rs 11,549 crore: ED |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/closely-guarded-mechanism-bandra-book-used-to-divert-rs-11549-crore-ed-10037431/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> Consequently, on 20 November 2019, the [[Reserve Bank of India]] (RBI) superseded the company's board, citing governance failures and payment defaults. This marked the first instance where the RBI invoked the [[Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016|Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code]] (IBC) against a financial services provider.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 June 2019 |title=DHFL tanks 16% after rating downgrade; what should investors do? |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/dhfl-tanks-16-after-rating-downgrade-what-should-investors-do-4067641.html |access-date=2019-06-07 |website=Moneycontrol}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mahesh |first=Prashant |date=2019-06-07 |title=Debt mutual funds take a tumble as DHFL slips on payment |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/mf/mf-news/debt-funds-take-a-tumble-as-dhfl-slips-on-payment/articleshow/69670067.cms |access-date=2019-06-07 |work=The Economic Times}}</ref>

=== Acquisition by Piramal and reorganization (2021–present) ===
The restructuring concluded in September 2021 when the Piramal Group acquired DHFL for a total consideration of ₹34,250 crore through the Committee of Creditors process.<ref name="lv">{{Cite news |date=29 September 2021 |title=Piramal Group completes DHFL acquisition in total consideration of ₹34,250 crore |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/piramal-group-completes-dhfl-acquisition-pays-rs-34-250-cr-as-total-consideration-11632892698017.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=4 June 2025}}</ref> As part of the resolution plan, Piramal Capital & Housing Finance Limited (PCHFL) was merged into DHFL via a reverse merger structure, with the merged entity continuing operations under the PCHFL name to leverage the existing branch network and customer base.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mishra |first=Lalatendu |date=2021-09-29 |title=Piramal group acquires DHFL, pays ₹14,700 crore in cash |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/piramal-group-acquires-dhfl-pays-14700-crore-in-cash/article36730639.ece |access-date=2026-05-14 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

In April 2025, the RBI approved the company's transition from a Housing Finance Company (HFC) to a [[NBFC and MFI in India|Non-Banking Financial Company – Investment and Credit Company]] (NBFC-ICC).<ref>{{cite news |date=8 April 2025 |title=Piramal Capital receives RBI nod to operate as NBFC-ICC |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/banking-finance-piramal-capital-receives-rbi-nod-to-operate-as-nbfc-icc-says-will-exit-housing-finance-biz-3801692/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CWe%20wish%20to%20inform%20you,of%20Non%2Dbanking%20Financial%20Institution%E2%80%93 |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref> The company subsequently surrendered its HFC license and was renamed Piramal Finance Limited to align with its strategic focus on retail and [[Small and medium enterprises|MSME]] lending. In May 2025, Piramal Enterprises Limited announced a proposed merger of Piramal Finance into the parent entity to improve capital efficiency.<ref>{{cite news |title=Piramal Enterprises to merge Piramal Finance with parent entity. |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/piramal-enterprises-to-merge-with-unlisted-housing-finance-arm-for-listing-124050900314_1.html |access-date=4 June 2025 |publisher=business-standard.com}}</ref> The reverse merger with Piramal Enterprises was completed in September 2025, resulting in a unified, publicly listed financial services entity.<ref>{{cite news |date=16 May 2025 |title=Piramal Enterprises approves merger of Piramal Finance |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/piramal-enterprises-approves-merger-of-piramal-finance/articleshow/110512983.cms |work=The Economic Times}}</ref>

== Operations ==
As of December 2025, Piramal Finance's total [[assets under management]] (AUM) reached ₹96,690 crore following its regulatory reclassification from a Housing Finance Company (HFC) to an Investment and Credit Company (NBFC-ICC).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Piramal Finance Reports ₹96,690 Crore AUM & Expands Retail Lending Share To 82% By FY26 |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/piramal-finance-reports-96690-crore-aum-expands-retail-lending-share-to-82-by-fy26 |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Free Press Journal |language=en}}</ref>

The retail division comprises approximately 82% of the total credit portfolio.<ref name=":1" /> This segment primarily consists of mortgage-backed loans, including residential housing finance and loans against property, with an average mortgage ticket size of ₹15 lakh focused on Tier II and Tier III cities. The retail division also includes [[Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006|micro, small, and medium enterprise]] (MSME) credit facilities, along with smaller portfolios in unsecured personal loans and used-vehicle financing.<ref name=":1" />

The wholesale division is managed under two distinct categories. The Wholesale 2.0 framework accounts for roughly 13% of the AUM. Established under a 2021 risk-management protocol to limit single-entity exposure, this framework provides construction finance to residential developers and term loans to mid-market corporate entities across smaller-scale projects. The remaining 5% of the AUM constitutes the legacy wholesale book. This portfolio consists of large-ticket real estate developer loans and stressed assets inherited from the 2021 acquisition of Dewan Housing Finance Corporation (DHFL), which are managed through a dedicated recovery and divestment process.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Piramal Enterprises Ltd. |url=https://www.hdfcsec.com/hsl.research.pdf/Initiating%20Coverage%20Piramal%20Enterprises%20-%2008062021.pdf |website=HDFC Secrities}}</ref>

The company operates a distribution network consisting of 518 branches located across 26 states and 429 cities.<ref name=":1" />

Operational funding is sourced through equity, domestic bank borrowings, and international credit lines. In early 2026, the firm secured a US$350 million financing agreement from the [[International Finance Corporation]] and the [[Asian Development Bank]] to support its affordable housing and MSME lending portfolios.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Piramal Finance raises $350 mn from IFC, ADB in first DFI deal |url=https://www.vccircle.com/piramalfinance-raises-350-mn-from-ifc-adb-in-first-dfi-deal |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=VCCircle |language=en-US}}</ref> Risk mitigation protocols rely on automated underwriting systems alongside co-lending partnerships with scheduled commercial banks to manage liquidity.<ref name=":2" />

==Subsidiaries==
===Pramerica life insurance===
Pramerica Life Insurance Limited is a joint venture between Piramal Capital and Housing Finance Limited (PCHFL) and Prudential International Insurance Holdings Ltd., a subsidiary of Prudential Financial, Inc., USA.<ref>{{cite web |title=DHFL owes ₹87,000 crore to banks and bondholders, including State Bank of India, Life Insurance Corp. of India, Union Bank of India and many other foreign and domestic lenders. |date=4 January 2021 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/business-news/oaktree-s-bid-for-dhfl-s-insurance-biz-faces-hurdle/story-akw9C7todTSgg2zDPTdI4N.html |publisher=[[Hindustan Times]]}}</ref> The company was established on September 1, 2008, as [[DLF (company)|DLF]] Pramerica Life Insurance Company Ltd. joint venture between DLF Limited & [[Prudential Financial]].<ref>{{cite web |title='Pramerica Life targets Rs 3,000-crore GWP in FY26,' Pankaj Gupta |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/money/pramerica-life-targets-rs-3000-crore-gwp-in-fy26-pankaj-gupta-3796945/ |publisher=[[The Financial Express (India)|Financialexpress]] |language=en |date=3 April 2025}}</ref>

==Legal matters and controversies==

=== SEBI insider-trading investigation ===
In 2024, the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] concluded a settlement with the former managing director of Piramal Capital & Housing Finance and associated parties in relation to an investigation into alleged [[insider trading]] in shares of [[Piramal Group|Piramal Enterprises]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Former Piramal Capital MD settles SEBI insider trading case |work=The Times of India |date=2024 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/piramal-capital-housing-finance-md-settles-sebi-probe/articleshow/112026867.cms |access-date=17 March 2026}}</ref> The settlement involved the payment of approximately ₹43.5 crore without admission or denial of wrongdoing under SEBI's settlement mechanism.<ref>{{cite news |title=Piramal co MD, two others pay RS 44 crore to settle Sebi probe |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/piramal-co-md-two-others-pay-rs-44-crore-to-settle-sebi-probe/articleshow/112026968.cms |access-date=17 March 2026 |work=The Times of India |date=26 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Piramal Capital Ex-MD Settles Insider Trading Case with Sebi |url=https://money.rediff.com/news/market/piramal-capital-ex-md-settles-insider-trading-case-with-sebi/13270320240725 |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Rediff |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=SEBI's Settlement Order In Piramal Insider Trading Case: All You Need To Know About The Terms |url=https://www.ndtvprofit.com/india/sebis-settlement-order-for-piramal-all-you-need-to-know-abouttheterms-9986771 |website=NDTV}}</ref>

=== Financial irregularities and probes against DHFL ===
In 2019, DHFL stopped payment of bonds and defaulted on its loan obligations. This caused its stock to fall over 97% and a government intervention in the company.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/company-stock/dewan-housing-finance-share-price-falls-icra-crisil/story/354114.html|title=Why Dewan Housing Finance share price fell up to 15% in early trade today|website=businesstoday.in|date=6 June 2019 |access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/dhfl-puts-fresh-deposits-and-renewals-on-hold-halts-pre-mature-withdrawals-1558460507432.html|title=DHFL puts fresh deposits and renewals on hold, halts pre-mature withdrawals|last=Borate|first=Neil|date=2019-05-21|website=Mint|language=en|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/dhfl-shares-slump-20-after-halting-fresh-public-deposits-1558497975452.html|title=DHFL falls nearly 10% as company stops accepting fresh deposits, halts renewals|last=Borate|first=Ravindra N. Sonavane, Neil|date=2019-05-22|website=Mint|language=en|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/govt-launches-probe-against-dhfl-issue-may-hit-sector-investment-119013101503_1.html|title=Govt launches probe against DHFL, issue may hit sector investment|last=Roy|first=Anup|date=2019-01-31|work=Business Standard India|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/company-stock/yes-bank-share-price-crashes-rs-1506-crore-net-loss-in-q4/story/341809.html|title=YES Bank share price loses 30% on surprise Rs 1,506-crore net loss in Q4|website=businesstoday.in|date=30 April 2019 |access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref>

In August 2019, as efforts to draft a resolution plan by restructuring DHFL debt into equity, a few of the DHFL bond holders moved to the debt recovery tribunal, which could impact the resolution process.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/use-of-insolvency-code-in-dewan-housing-will-expedite-resolution-process-1569212343590.html|title=Use of insolvency code in Dewan Housing will expedite resolution process|last=Ghosh|first=Shayan|date=2019-09-23|website=Mint|language=en|access-date=2019-09-23}}</ref> The company meanwhile offered to repay all investors in full with due process of inter-creditor-agreement.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/dhfl-offers-to-repay-investors-in-full-but-seeks-nod-for-ica/articleshow/71344455.cms|title=DHFL offers to repay investors in full, but seeks nod for ICA|last1=Das|first1=Saikat|date=2019-09-28|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2019-09-28|last2=Rebello|first2=Joel}}</ref>

In October 2019, the [[Enforcement Directorate]] conducted raids at several places of DHFL offices and promoter residences and found links of money laundering activity in loans given to firms closely linked to the promoters of the company.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/companies/debt-laden-dhfl-loaned-to-firms-tied-to-its-promoters-ed-probe-6079523/|title=Debt-laden DHFL loaned to firms tied to its promoters: ED probe|date=2019-10-21|website=The Indian Express|language=en-IN|access-date=2019-10-21}}</ref> Additionally the trail of the loan given by DHFL to Sunblink real estate in 2010 lead to gangster Iqbal Mirchi, an accomplice of the organized crime mastermind Dawood Ibrahim.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/dhfl-lent-rs-2186-crore-to-company-under-lens-for-mirchi-links-ed-investigations-reveal/articleshow/71623886.cms|title=DHFL News: DHFL lent Rs 2,186 crore to company under lens for Mirchi links, ED investigations reveal|newspaper=The Economic Times}}</ref>

On 20 November 2019, under Section 45-IE (I) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Indian central bank removed the board of directors of Dewan Housing Finance Corporation Limited (DHFL). The reasons cited by the banking regulator for the dismissal of the DHFL board of directors were: inadequate governance and the various defaults on its payment obligations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=48684|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200213085754/https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=48684|archive-date = 13 February 2020|title = Reserve Bank of India - Press Releases}}</ref>

On 27 January 2020, the promoter of DHFL, Kapil Wadhawan was arrested under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The arrest was connected to his firm's alleged involvement in providing loans to the organized criminal enterprise of Dawood Ibrahim.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/dhfl-promoter-kapil-wadhawan-arrested-in-iqbal-mirchi-money-laundering-case/story-Pdouu5NbIzEhn6c27YD3cM.html|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200214184318/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/dhfl-promoter-kapil-wadhawan-arrested-in-iqbal-mirchi-money-laundering-case/story-Pdouu5NbIzEhn6c27YD3cM.html|archive-date = 14 February 2020|title = DHFL promoter Kapil Wadhawan arrested in Iqbal Mirchi money laundering case|date = 27 January 2020}}</ref> On 22 February 2020, the PMLA court granted bail to Kapil Wadhwan. The Bombay high court upheld the bail decision by PMLA court, rejecting Indian [[Enforcement Directorate]] requests to stay the bail application.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/cricket-matches-in-wankhede-to-disrupt-normal-traffic-in-south-mumbai/story-3azJrE5TQE5g7DF7oVOosJ.html|title = Cricket matches in Wankhede to disrupt normal traffic in South Mumbai|date = 8 March 2020}}</ref>

The ED has linked [[Yes Bank]] for various fraud and transactions amounting to 3700 crores as debentures in DHFL. The central bank appointed administrator at Dewan Housing Finance (DHFL) has ordered a transaction audit at the non-bank lender after allegations of money laundering surfaced in the aftermath of the regulatory action on Yes Bank.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/yes-bank-founder-rana-kapoors-wife-daughter-charged-by-cbi-in-alleged-bribery-case-2192282|title=Crisis-Hit Yes Bank Founder Rana Kapoor's Wife, Daughters Charged By CBI|website=NDTV.com|access-date=2020-03-13}}</ref>

On 24 March 2021, [[Central Bureau of Investigation|CBI]] filed a new suit against DHFL and its promoters Kapil Wadhawan and Dheeraj Wadhawan, wherein the later were accused of syphoning off the welfare subsidy fund of [[Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana]] by creating 260,000 fake home loan accounts under the same scheme under the guise of a non-existent branch.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2021-03-24|title=CBI books DHFL over fake accounts created in PMAY|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/cbi-books-dhfl-over-fake-accounts-created-in-pmay-11616608277393.html|access-date=2021-03-25|website=mint|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=DHFL Share Price Hits Lower Circuit After CBI Books Promoters For Creating Fake Accounts|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/stocks/dhfl-share-price-hits-lower-circuit-after-cbi-books-promoters-for-creating-fake-accounts-6691161.html|access-date=2021-03-25|website=Moneycontrol|date=25 March 2021 }}</ref> The suit says, fake loans were granted worth ₹14,046 crore of which ₹11,755.79 crore were routed to shell corporations and citing these loans, subsidy amounts were claimed under [[Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-03-24|title=CBI books DHFL for creating over 2 lakh fake home loan accounts under PMAY|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/cbi-books-dhfl-for-creating-over-2-lakh-fake-home-loan-accounts-under-pmay-101616592758747.html|access-date=2021-03-25|website=Hindustan Times|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=DHFL directors availed thousands of crores through fake loan accounts under PMAY: CBI|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/current/economy-politics/dhfl-directors-availed-thousands-of-crores-through-fake-loan-accounts-under-pmjay-cbi/story/434782.html|access-date=2021-03-25|website=www.businesstoday.in|date=24 March 2021 }}</ref>

In September 2025, the [[Enforcement Directorate]] (ED) attached DHFL assets worth {{INRConvert|186|c}} in a bank fraud case.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-10 |title=DHFL loan fraud case: ED attaches assets worth ₹185.84 cr |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/dhfl-loan-fraud-case-ed-attaches-assets-worth-185-84-cr-101757445066053.html |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>
